name: dropdown-menu
title: Dropdown Menu
description: Row actions, filters, and view settings behind one button.

## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dropdown-menu ``` The examples compose `@cadence/button`; install that item alongside the menu when copying them. **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react lucide-react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | dropdown-menu | `@components/cadence/dropdown-menu/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/dropdown-menu.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: dropdown-menu](https://cadence.dev/r/dropdown-menu.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all nine target files, including every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. The provider files and `motion` are required imports; wrapping your application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. These payloads contain no additional menu-specific CSS or assets. Usage, the top specimen and every body example also compose Button. Follow [Button's manual installation](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation) and copy its full [payload source](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json), adding `@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` alongside the shared files already listed. Its only additional npm dependency is: ```package-manager npm install class-variance-authority ``` Logical placement uses `DirectionProvider` from the already required `@base-ui/react`; pair its direction with the DOM `dir` attribute, as shown. In Next.js App Router, keep Usage, Items, shortcuts, and destructive actions, Checkbox and radio items, Submenus, Grouping and Controlled open in client modules: they own state and handlers. Disabled controls, Placement, Alignment, Logical placement, Non-modal menu and Explicit motion scopes are static compositions and can be rendered by a Server Component using serializable props, including the JSX element passed to `render`. Adding event handlers, refs or function-valued `render`, `className` or `style` props requires a client caller. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup; hydrated opening, navigation, selection and dismissal require JavaScript. Compose a root, trigger and content. Pass Button through the trigger's `render` prop so the primitive's accessible name, expanded state and events reach the actual button. Content already includes its portal, positioner and popup; do not add a second portal around it. Its defaults are bottom/start with a 4px side offset and zero alignment offset. Submenus use Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent; their defaults are right/start, zero side offset and -3px alignment offset. Base UI owns collision handling, item focus, typeahead, submenu navigation and dismissal. Cap caller-defined widths for narrow viewports and verify the actual open panel bounds. In Placement, the fixed `w-52` can overflow a narrow side placement; add `max-w-(--available-width)` and check the minimum width too. The caller owns commands and their effects, permissions, controlled `open`, checkbox `checked` and radio-group `value`, persistence and error feedback. Use `defaultOpen`, `defaultChecked` and `defaultValue` for uncontrolled initial state. For external opening, Controlled open pairs a unique root `triggerId` with the trigger's `id` to preserve the anchor. Put actions on `onClick`; ordinary items close by default, `closeOnClick={false}` keeps them open, and checkbox/radio items stay open by default. Disabled items expose their state and remain discoverable with arrow keys but cannot activate. Shortcut text does not register a key binding. Group labels name a DropdownMenuGroup; ungrouped labels are captions. This menu supplies no form-state or validation package, and the examples only update local status text. Full mode scales and fades the popup and animates the checkbox/radio mark. Reduced keeps opacity and removes scale; none disables those transitions from the first mounted frame. A nested provider can restore full inside none, subject to the system reduced-motion preference. Keep native menu focus and dismissal behavior when supplying custom render elements or handlers; use ordinary links or Navigation Menu for a navigation list and Popover for a task form. ## Usage ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu"; export function RowActions() { const [result, setResult] = useState("No action yet"); return (

Base UI keeps disabled items keyboard-focusable so their unavailable state can be discovered. The width cap follows Base UI's available-width variable so the panel fits the chosen side on a narrow viewport. ```tsx "use client"; import { DirectionProvider } from "@base-ui/react/direction-provider"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu"; export function LogicalMenus() { return (

Use a popover when the panel contains a task form. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu"; export function MenuModality() { return (

Popup and checkbox indicator both use that local clock. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu"; export function MenuMotionScopes() { return (
}>Open without motion Comments }>Open nested full Comments
); } ``` ## When to use - A row of actions behind one trigger: a table row, a card, a file. - A filter or view setting where the panel stays open while several options change. - A command list too long for a toolbar and too short to need search. ## When not to use - A list of links for ordinary site navigation. Use a `navigation-menu` or plain links; a navigational command in a menu retains the menu's keyboard behavior. - A value you select and read back. Use `select`, which keeps the chosen value in the trigger. - A destructive answer that must be confirmed. Use `alert-dialog`; a menu item is a one-keystroke action and closes immediately. - More than about a dozen entries, or entries the user has to search. Use `command`. ## API ### `DropdownMenu` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | -------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- | | `open` | `boolean` | – | Controlled open state. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state. | | `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | – | Fires on every open and close, including Escape. | | `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Limits outside pointer interaction and locks desktop scrolling. Tab dismisses the menu. | ### `DropdownMenuTrigger` Native button props and `render`. The trigger owns `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; pass a `Button` through `render` rather than wrapping one, so those land on the element the user presses. ### `DropdownMenuContent` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | `side` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"bottom"` | Preferred side; flips when there is no room. | | `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Alignment along the trigger's edge. | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `4` | Gap between trigger and panel, in pixels. | | `alignOffset` | `number` | `0` | Shift along the alignment axis. | | `className` | string or Base UI state callback | – | Merged last. | ### `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | Part | Props | Notes | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | | `DropdownMenuItem` | `onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`, `closeOnClick` | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`. | | `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `inset` | Keeps the menu open. | | `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | One selection for the group. | | `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | `value` (required), `disabled`, `inset` | Keeps the menu open. | | `DropdownMenuSub` | – | Groups a submenu trigger and its content. | | `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | `disabled`, `inset` | Renders the chevron. | | `DropdownMenuSubContent` | Same as `DropdownMenuContent` | `side="right"`, `alignOffset={-3}` by default. | ### `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator` `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuShortcut`, `DropdownMenuPortal`. ## Motion contract | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- | | open | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) | | close | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes | | check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale` | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | – | – | Opening and closing are one CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale`, driven by Base UI's `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`, so an interrupted close reverses rather than restarts. The panel grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger; a submenu grows out of its item the same way, because both levels render the same panel. The highlighted row is a colour change, not motion: `data-highlighted` switches the item's background. A travelling highlight would be a shared element across items — `layout.move`, which belongs to `tabs` and `toggle-group`, not to a menu that can be entered at any row. Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside `none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the first mounted frame. The site header changes the inherited mode on the same component tree; the named Explicit motion scopes example demonstrates fixed local overrides. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup remain owned by the primitive. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Enter` / `Space` / `ArrowDown` | Opens the menu and highlights the first item. | | `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Moves the highlight; it wraps at the ends. | | `Home` / `End` | First and last item. | | Typeahead letters | Highlights the next item whose label starts with them. | | `Enter` / `Space` | Runs the highlighted item and closes the menu. | | `ArrowRight` | Opens the highlighted submenu; `ArrowLeft` closes it. | | `Escape` | Closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger, runs nothing. | | `Tab` | Closes the menu and moves to the next control in the page. | ## Accessibility - Base UI wires the trigger with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and renders the panel as `role="menu"` with `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, and `menuitemradio` parts. - For a navigational command, use `DropdownMenuItem render={}`. The anchor keeps its `href` and receives `role="menuitem"` and Base UI's focus and activation behavior. Do not nest a second interactive link inside an item. - `DropdownMenuLabel` inside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is the group's accessible name. Outside a group it is a caption: visible to sighted users, not announced as a label. - `DropdownMenuShortcut` is text, not a binding. Announce the shortcut in the item's label only when it is registered, or the reader is told about a key that does nothing. - The default modal mode limits outside pointer interaction and locks desktop scrolling. `Tab` still dismisses the menu and continues the page order; this is not a dialog focus trap. ## Responsive behavior The panel caps at `--available-height` and scrolls. The positioner can flip the side and shift along the cross axis, but caller-defined widths can still exceed the available space in side placements. Cap them with `max-w-(--available-width)` and verify open bounds; reduce the `min-w-[8rem]` minimum too if the available space is narrower. On touch, the menu opens on tap and the highlighted item follows the tap; there is no hover state to design around. `min-w-[8rem]` keeps short menus readable, and the panel does not stretch to the trigger's width — a menu is as wide as its widest item. ## Performance - One portal per open menu; closing unmounts it after the exit transition. - The panel animates `opacity` and `scale` only, on one element. Nothing measures layout, and no JavaScript runs per frame. - Items carry no per-item motion: the only animated state is the check mark, and it animates two properties on a 14px span. - Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). A page with a dozen closed menus pays for one component's source, no mounted popups, and no timers. ## Notes for AI - Put the action on `onClick`. Base UI's menu item has no `onSelect`; a handler that only exists on `onSelect` never fires. - Pass the trigger through `render` so `aria-haspopup` lands on the button, not on a wrapper. - Group items before labelling them: a `DropdownMenuLabel` outside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is a caption, and a group without a label is announced as an unnamed group. - Do not put a form with validation inside a menu. A menu is a list of commands; `popover` is the surface for controls. The popup owns its `duration.fast` clock, including provider timeScale and the reduced duration multiplier. An explicit full provider restores the clock inside an outer none scope. In none mode the popup removes starting/ending opacity and uses zero duration on the first frame. Function-valued popup `className` and `style` receive Base UI state and merge after the component defaults.
